concept.name: Every room began as a brief
concept.idea: A homeowner walks the Parade and sees finished rooms; she never sees how they came together: the brief, the choices, the questions from the site. The Moll Drive house is Leah's work at Middle West Studio, built by a Sauk City crew that frames, finishes and builds its own millwork. The batch tells her, honestly and from the finished side, what working with Middle West Studio looks like: bring your own house to Leah, and the two of you work from one page, from brief to install, so you always see the same direction your designer does. This house was designed and built before that page was ready (it was NOT run in Patina); it is the kind of house Middle West will work on with her, from one shared page, going forward. Three angles from the brief, one per surface: the decisions you can't see from the doorway (P01, P04, P07); the warm wood, one piece, the drawing and the crew behind it (P02); ask for Leah, a designer talking with a homeowner standing in a finished kitchen (P03, P05, P06). The seed copy's facts, schedule and every ⟨FILL⟩ stay; its studio angle and designer asks are rewritten for the homeowner, with Leah at middlewest.studio as the only ask.
concept.artDirection: Real, credited photographs of the Moll Drive house or the builder's rendering (credited 'Rendering: Kippley Custom Carpentry'), no people, daylight through real windows: a room from the doorway, the woodwork's grain up close, the front of the house in late afternoon. Paper ground (#EDE9E4), Playfair Display headlines in sentence case, Inter body, DM Mono eyebrow carrying the place and date line (Waunakee · Fall Parade · Oct 9–11 and 16–18). Instagram: image owns the top two thirds, headline on paper below, text out of the outer 64 px. Poster: one image, one Playfair line readable from six feet; J04 is the only image that may be generated, a warm oak and brass texture that carries the label 'Illustration' on the print and is never captioned or described as the house; a real credited detail photo may replace it. One-pagers: eyebrow, Playfair title, one image band, three or four single-column sections, CTA at the foot (Leah at Middle West Studio, middlewest.studio), print-safe. Email: letter first, from Leah, at most one photo under the opening paragraph, readable with images off. Flat paper, ink and clay-beige hairlines; no gradients, no badges, no red/green, no product screenshots, no Patina mark as hero.
